## Choosing n_bins

Reconstruction error is the mean absolute difference between a value and the value its bin decodes to -- a point mass decodes to itself, any other bin to its midpoint -- as a share of the channel's interquartile range on the training values. `train` is measured on the values the edges were fitted on, `val` on the validation split (2021), which they never saw. `bins` is the number a channel uses: fewer than the candidate only where point masses took exact bins.

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| n_bins chosen | 256 |
| why | Unchanged from v0's finding: reconstruction error falls with every doubling on every channel, on the validation split as on the training values, so the grid has no interior optimum and the finest candidate is chosen. It costs 256 of the bin block's 1,024 fixed identifiers (ADR-0003) and nothing in sequence length, one token per channel per step at any bin count. What changes at v1 is how the 256 are spent, not how many there are: 32 go to the fixed-width tails, so the quantile middle has 32 fewer and a slightly higher median error, and the tails are no longer coarse. v0's claim that 256 bins leave "about 13,000 training values" a bin was a plain division and was corrected in ADR-0011; the report measures the occupancy of every tail bin rather than dividing. |

Read the smaller candidates with care. The tails take 32 bins whatever the budget is, which is 64: 50%, 128: 25%, 256: 12% of it, so a candidate below the chosen one is not the like-for-like comparison M1b made -- it is a different rule as well as a smaller budget. The bin count is not reopened here (ADR-0011); the comparison that matters for the tail rule is the quantile-only fit at the chosen count, below.

## Point masses at n_bins = 256

A value holding at least 1/n_bins of a channel's training values would fill a whole quantile bin by itself; each such value has an exact bin, reaching halfway to its nearest observed neighbours, and decodes to itself.

## The tails: 16 fixed-width bins a side

Every channel gets 16 fixed-width bins below the training p0.5% and 16 above the p99.5%, after the point masses take their exact bins; the rest of the bin budget is quantiles over the middle. `quantile only` is the same bin count fitted the M1b way on the same values, so the two columns differ by the tail rule and nothing else.
